text:
alex_k: Heads up — prospect GlacierBox sent over a SIG/CAIQ and is asking to start a POC next week. They want to connect via VPC peering and request long-term object store access. Link: https://glacierbox.example/caiq.pdf

lina_s: thx. do we have the intake form filled? curious what data classes they'll touch (PII/health/financial?)

sam_sales: sales note: POC will use dev data (no real PII) per customer, but eventual rollout may include customer-uploaded files. timeline is tight — they want creds by Mon.

maria_proc: we haven't onboarded GlacierBox before. procurement needs SOC2 + at least one attestation. CAIQ is great but we need answers for encryption key ownership and subprocessor list.

josh_legal: +1 on subprocessors. also we need explicit contract language for breach notification (48hr) and right to audit for Tier 1 vendors.

infra-bot: Reminder: please complete vendor-intake form at https://redwood-internal.example/vendor-intake within 48h or the request will be flagged.

alex_k: Lina — can you triage the CAIQ? key questions: KMS control (CSPM vs CMK), network access (VPC peering vs public endpoints), and retention/snapshot policies.

lina_s: scanning quick — CAIQ shows AES-256 at rest and TLS1.2 in transit. key management unclear (mentions provider-managed keys). I'll flag for CMK if customer will upload sensitive files.

sam_sales: POC team says CMK not required for initial trial, but enterprise deals will require CMK or HSM support. can we offer a temp mitigation (isolated bucket + short TTL creds)?

lina_s: mitigation idea: require scoped IAM role + ephemeral creds (aws sts assume-role for each session) and strict VPC allowlist. Also require server-side encryption with provider key until CMK is available.

josh_legal: please capture that as an interim control in the contract addendum: "Vendor will provide scoped, time-limited credentials and maintain audit logs for all object access; full CMK support will be delivered by [date]".

maria_proc: procurement requests the subprocessors list and current SOC2 report before we grant any network access. can sales share the CAIQ + SOC2 link with me?

sam_sales: sharing now — https://files.glacierbox.example/soc2-2025.pdf and CAIQ link in my earlier message. Sending to procurement DM.

lina_s: technical ask for infra: what's the required network setup for the POC? VPC peering needs routing and firewall rules. prefer not to do cross-account peering for a short POC.

alex_k: prefer we do NAT'd egress to their public endpoint plus strict egress rules and logging — avoids peering setup. if performance hits SLA we can revisit peering.

infra-bot: Note: any peering request triggers a security review and longer lead time (2-3 days).

lina_s: action items: 1) I'll finish CAIQ triage and flag CMK + logging controls (by EOD). 2) Maria — need SOC2 + subprocessors. 3) Josh — draft interim contract language for scoped creds and audit logs. 4) Alex/Sales — opt for public endpoint + ephemeral creds for POC to avoid peering.

sam_sales: sounds good. i'll ask GlacierBox to restrict the POC dataset to non-production/dev data and confirm subprocessors. i'll loop procurement on the SOC2 doc.

josh_legal: I'll draft the clause and post in this thread when ready.

alex_k: thanks all — if anyone needs me to join the intake call tomorrow ping me. :thumbsup:

lina_s: quick note: CAIQ shows incomplete answers under "Key Management" and "Logging and Monitoring". I'll add questions: - do they publish KMS rotation policy? - where do audit logs ship (S3/3rd party SIEM)? - retention length?

maria_proc: once we get SOC2 and subprocessors, procurement will issue a provisional access form and tie it to the scoped creds.

sam_sales: I'll aim to get everything to you by EOD today. thanks! :pray:
